Smallest effect a uSDT study detects

Source: R/plan.R
usdt_mdes.Rd

Finds, for each hypothesis, the smallest effect that a design detects with the given power: the population value of the tested quantity, moved away from H0 with the other values of the population fixed, at which the approximate power of usdt_power() reaches it. For an equivalence test (in), it finds the narrowest equivalence region, around the same centre, that the design can establish.

Usage

usdt_mdes(
  population,
  subjects,
  trials,
  hypothesis = c("diff = 0", "rho = 0", "intercept = 0"),
  power = 0.8,
  alpha = 0.05,
  signal = 0.5,
  dichotomize = c("none", "influence", "awareness", "both"),
  vary = NULL,
  range = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'usdt_mdes'
print(x, digits = 3L, ...)

Arguments

population

A usdt_population object, or a usdt_plan from usdt_plan(), whose designs, hypotheses and settings are then used.

subjects

Number of subjects. Several values give one design each.

trials

Number of trials per subject in each task, signal and noise trials together: one value for both tasks, or one for each as c(awareness = , influence = ) or list(awareness = , influence = ). Several values give one design each. A value shared by both tasks keeps them equal, and values given for each task are crossed.

hypothesis

Character vector of hypotheses, written as in usdt_equivalence(): "<quantity> <op> <value>" with the quantity diff, rho, slope or intercept and the operator =, < or >, or "<quantity> in [a, b]" and "<quantity> out [a, b]". The default tests the three point nulls that hsdt() reports.

power

Power to reach (default 0.80).

alpha

Significance level of every test, between 0 and 0.5 (default 0.05).

signal

Proportion of signal trials in each task (default 0.5), one value for both tasks or one for each. Each task must have a whole number of signal and of noise trials.

dichotomize

Which tasks are split at the median, as in usdt_data_tasks(): "none", "influence", "awareness", "both", or one logical value for each task. The split fixes the criterion of a task at zero, so its criterion values in population are not used.

vary

Optional name of the population value to move instead of the tested quantity: "mu_A", "mu_I", "sigma_A", "sigma_I", "rho", "intercept", "criterion_A", "criterion_I", "sd_criterion_A" or "sd_criterion_I". Needs range.

range

With vary, the interval of values to search, c(from, to). The result is the value nearest to from that reaches the power.

x

A usdt_mdes object.

digits

Number of decimals printed.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class usdt_mdes: a data frame with one row per scenario, design and hypothesis, and the columns scenario, subjects, trials_awareness, trials_influence, hypothesis, varies (the value moved), population (its value in the population), power_population (the power there) and mdes (the value at which the power is reached, or NA if it is not reached in the range searched). For an equivalence test, varies is "margin" and mdes the half-width of the narrowest region. The attribute curve holds the power over the values searched.

Details

Moving a quantity keeps the other values of the population fixed as its parameterization says (see usdt_population()): the difference moves the influence mean with the awareness mean fixed. The intercept moves the influence mean with the means and SDs and the correlation fixed. The correlation (and the slope, through it) keeps both means under the correlation parameterization and the intercept under the latent regression. The search runs from the value of H0 (or the nearest bound) outwards, in the direction of H1, and the power along the way comes from the same draws of the sample mean and covariance as in usdt_power(), so it can level off below the target when fits on the boundary are frequent. The result is then NA.

See also

usdt_power(), usdt_plan()

Examples

pop <- usdt_population(dprime    = c(awareness = 0.15, influence = 0.30),
                       sd_dprime = c(awareness = 0.35, influence = 0.30),
                       cor_dprime = 0.3, criterion = 0.1)

usdt_mdes(pop, subjects = 80, trials = c(awareness = 64, influence = 200),
          dichotomize = "influence")
#> ── Smallest detectable effect ─────────────────────── approximate · power 0.8 ── 
#> 
#>   Design       80 subjects; trials per subject: 64 Awareness, 200 Influence
#> 
#>   Hypothesis        Varies     Population  Power there  Smallest
#>   H1 Δd' = 0        diff            0.150        0.712     0.168
#>   H2 rho = 0        rho             0.300        0.379     0.499
#>   H3 intercept = 0  intercept       0.261        0.992     0.135
#> 
#>   Approximate power, as in usdt_power(). NA: the power is not reached 
#>   in the range searched.

# The narrowest equivalence margin for the difference
usdt_mdes(update(pop, dprime = c(awareness = 0.15, influence = 0.15)),
          subjects = 80, trials = c(awareness = 64, influence = 200),
          hypothesis = "diff in [-0.2, 0.2]", dichotomize = "influence")
#> ── Smallest detectable effect ─────────────────────── approximate · power 0.8 ── 
#> 
#>   Design       80 subjects; trials per subject: 64 Awareness, 200 Influence
#> 
#>   Hypothesis             Varies  Population  Power there  Smallest
#>   H1 Δd' in [-0.2, 0.2]  margin       0.000        0.913     0.175
#> 
#>   Approximate power, as in usdt_power(). NA: the power is not reached 
#>   in the range searched.
#>   For an equivalence test, the smallest value is the half-width of the
#>   narrowest region the design can establish.

# The SD of the awareness d' the intercept test needs
usdt_mdes(pop, subjects = 80, trials = c(awareness = 64, influence = 200),
          hypothesis = "intercept > 0", vary = "sigma_A",
          range = c(0.05, 0.6), dichotomize = "influence")
#> ── Smallest detectable effect ─────────────────────── approximate · power 0.8 ── 
#> 
#>   Design       80 subjects; trials per subject: 64 Awareness, 200 Influence
#> 
#>   Hypothesis        Varies   Population  Power there  Smallest
#>   H3 intercept > 0  sigma_A       0.350        0.995     0.217
#> 
#>   Approximate power, as in usdt_power(). NA: the power is not reached 
#>   in the range searched.
